calls.head: A shadow job for Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Hagel’s line (Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Red Wings’ first line is DeBrincat, Finnie and Arvidsson.

DET.head: We gave Detroit only a 31% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Detroit got the good looks
surprises.body: Detroit’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay buried Detroit in shots
surprises.body: Tampa Bay throws more pucks at the net than almost anyone. Even by those standards, this was lopsided: Tampa Bay took 57 of the 84 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Tampa Bay would expect about 54%. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Detroit brought the hits
surprises.body: Detroit usually hits more than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 174 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 107 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Point has two goals as the Lightning get past the Red Wings
paras: Brayden Point opened the scoring for the Lightning on the power play early in the first. The Red Wings went more than 18 minutes without a shot on goal, from midway through the first to early in the second, while the Lightning put 13 on net. Point scored again midway through the first to make it 2-0 for the Lightning. Detroit pulled John Gibson after two goals and turned to Daniil Tarasov to start the second. Anthony Cirelli stretched the lead to 3-0 midway through the second, and that one stood up as the winner. Lucas Raymond got the Red Wings on the board less than two minutes later, and J.T. Compher cut Tampa Bay’s lead to 3-2 on the power play early in the third. Ryan McDonagh shut the door with an empty-netter with just one second left.

The Lightning had the better of the chances, outshooting the Red Wings 27-21 (21-13 at 5-on-5). Andrei Vasilevskiy made 19 saves for the Bolts. The Lightning improved to 9-3-2 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Red Wings dropped to 7-6-3, still last in the Atlantic.

items.text: Brayden Point has a point in five straight games.
The Lightning have beaten the Red Wings four straight times, going back to last season.
Ryan McDonagh scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 22 (25 games played since).
Emil Lilleberg was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Max Crozier played instead.
